content:
- Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in early periods of the 30-day window.
- Forecasts show a strong upward trend (increasing) while true outcomes often exhibit volatility or mean-reversion, particularly after spikes.
- After a sharp price spike, model forecasts overshoot and fail to correct downward — suggesting lack of momentum decay modeling.
- Model fails to capture downward corrections after high true values; tends to hold or slightly increase forecast despite evidence of mean reversion.
- Forecasts are too smooth; fail to reflect recent volatility or sudden drops in true outcomes.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward lower values, especially when true values are above 70–75; may be underweighting supply/demand shocks.
- In cases where true values are rising sharply, model lags behind and doesn’t adjust quickly enough — suggesting poor lag correction or delayed response to new data.
- Model overfits to recent low values, leading to persistent underestimation even when true values are recovering.
